Parysow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Starowola, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Parysów developed through the 19th century; by 1921, 1,906 Jews made up 56% of the village's population, most murdered at Treblinka in September 1942. The cemetery's exact founding is unknown, though Tzadik Jehoszua Asher Rabinowicz, founder of a local Hasidic dynasty, was buried here in 1862 beneath an ohel. During WWII, victims from the Stoczek Łukowski ghetto and deportations were buried here as the site was devastated; postwar, grave-robbers dug for gold dental crowns and the site became a sand mine and illegal dump. In 2012-2013, New Yorker Duvid Singer and an anonymous Polish donor funded rebuilding the tzadik's ohel; the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage fenced the site with the ESJF in 2015.
